records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.flora_name: Linum rigidum Pursh var. berlandieri (Hook.) Torr. & A.Gray

characters.habit: 1999 parent L. rigidum: glabrous erect/ascending annual to 40 cm, branched above
characters.leaves: Linear-lanceolate or lanceolate, acute, 1–4.1 mm wide, usually bearing stipular glands
characters.flowers: Deep yellow petals with large red-brown basal area, usually 13–16 mm; sepals 7–9 mm
characters.fruit: Thick-walled, opaque, broadly ovoid, sharply tapering to flattened base
characters.habitat: Wide Texas distribution; often Blackland Prairie and westward
characters.phenology: Parent species mid-April to early June

records.diagnostics: Opaque thick-walled fruits and stipular glands vs translucent thin-walled fruits without glands in var. rigidum
holds: TAXONOMIC HOLD: inventory treats species L. berlandieri, flora treats variety of L. rigidum; retain both concepts, do not merge or double-count distribution
1999 explicitly discusses hybridization/introgression underlying varietal treatment

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Annual 5–30 cm, glabrous except hairy angular upper stems
characters.leaves: Linear/linear-lanceolate, 10 mm or shorter; upper leaf edges not ciliate
characters.flowers: Yellow sometimes red basal zone; petals 8–12 mm per key
characters.fruit: Species-specific mature fruit dimensions not stated in account
characters.habitat: Sandy/gravelly sites, West Texas to Post Oak Savannah

records.diagnostics: Upper stem hairs only on angles and upper blades without marginal hairs; vs L. imbricatum with ciliate upper bracts and overlapped leaves
holds: Detailed fruit/seed measurements require external FNA source verification

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Glabrous appearing low annual 3–30 cm, often several stems, sparingly branched near top
characters.leaves: Short overlapping leaves, 5–10 mm long per key; upper foliage and bracts show sparse conspicuous ciliate margins
characters.stems: Upper stems and pedicels minutely short-hirsute
characters.flowers: Yellow sometimes red-brown basal area, petals 6.5–8 mm

records.diagnostics: Tightly imbricated small leaves and hairs along upper leaf/bract margins, unlike mostly hairless-edged L. hudsonioides
holds: Flora species summary calls glabrous despite key mentioning localized upper stem and bract hairs; record scope of hairs rather than treat as contradiction

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.flora_name: Linum rigidum Pursh (var. rigidum and var. berlandieri separated in 1999 flora)

characters.habit: Glabrous stiff erect/ascending annual to 40 cm, widely branched above
characters.leaves: Var. rigidum: linear acute/acuminate, 1–2 mm wide, no stipular glands
characters.flowers: Showy petals (9–)12–16(–19) mm species-wide; var. rigidum typically 12–14 mm coppery-yellow/orange with basal red lines or short reddish basal area
characters.fruit: Species-wide 3.5–4.7 mm; var. rigidum thin-walled translucent elliptic with rounded base and visible dark seeds; var. berlandieri thick-walled opaque ovoid
characters.habitat: Rocky or sandy open prairies/disturbed lands

records.diagnostics: Compare var. rigidum vs L. berlandieri using fruits' translucency and stipular glands rather than yellow petal color
holds: Species inventory includes separate L. berlandieri; high risk of double-counting specimens with 1999 broader L. rigidum concept
Toxicity reported as livestock poison; no direct plant-handling recommendation

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Glabrous perennial 20–70 cm, several stems from hardened perennial base (1999 key)
characters.leaves: Linear, lower leaves alternate or opposite; leaf bases generally with stipular glands, sepals glandular-toothed
characters.flowers: Clear yellow petals; 6–10 mm per key, separate styles
characters.fruit: Fruit opening into ten one-seeded segments (1999 key)
characters.habitat: Limestone outcrops, mainly Trans-Pecos to Edwards Plateau and north-central Texas

records.diagnostics: Perennial with woody thickened stem base and clear yellow 6–10-mm petals; compares to annual stiff flax
holds: Specific fruit/seed size and reliable photographs still needed; do not extrapolate from related species

notes: One species and its historical varietal treatment deliberately overlap for reconciliation; not county approved; photos, attributions and live site unchanged.
